What

What Fruit Tree Pruning & Maintenance Involves

Fruit tree pruning is yield-driven work — done right, it improves fruit quality, increases light penetration to the fruiting wood, and keeps the harvest at a manageable height. Apples and pears follow a modified central-leader system; peaches and tart cherries follow open-center training. Most NE Ohio fruit trees benefit from annual maintenance pruning in late winter, February to early March, with optional summer pruning for size control.

The distinction that matters: fruit trees are pruned for production, not just shape. Aaron and the crew remove crossing and inward-growing branches, head back the leader, and thin fruiting wood so the tree carries a clean, well-lit crop. Disease management — apple scab, fire blight, cedar-apple rust — is a routine part of the same visit. Every fruit tree job starts with a free written estimate before you commit.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Growers Call Roubic

The top fruit tree scenarios Aaron walks each season across NE Ohio properties.

Annual Apple & Pear Maintenance

Modified central-leader trees need yearly late-winter pruning to keep fruiting wood lit and the harvest at a reachable height.

Peach Open-Center Training

Peaches fruit on previous-year wood and need more aggressive, structured pruning around three or four scaffold branches.

Disease Showing in the Crown

Apple scab, fire blight, or cedar-apple rust every spring means the tree needs sanitation pruning with sterilized tools.

Neglected or Overgrown Orchard

Trees that haven't been touched in years crop poorly. Staged renewal pruning brings structure and yield back over a season or two.

Common Fruit Tree Questions

Fruit Tree Pruning & Maintenance FAQ

Five things NE Ohio growers want to know before booking.

When is the best time to prune my apple tree?
Late winter — February to early March — before bud break. Summer pruning in June or July is acceptable for size control on vigorous trees, but the main structural and fruiting-wood pruning belongs in late winter.
Why does my apple tree look bad every spring?
Most likely apple scab (a fungal disease) or cedar-apple rust if you have cedars nearby. Sanitation pruning to remove affected wood helps; severe cases may benefit from a fungicide program, and removing host cedars is an option for cedar-apple rust.
Should I prune my peach tree the same way as my apple tree?
No. Peaches use an open-center system with no central leader and are pruned more aggressively because they fruit on previous-year wood. Apples and pears use a modified central-leader system. We match the method to the species on every visit.
How much does fruit tree pruning cost?
Fruit tree pruning typically runs $150–$400 per tree depending on size and scope. Multi-tree orchard contracts qualify for package savings — Aaron confirms the price during the free on-site estimate.
Can pruning fix fire blight on my apple or pear tree?
Pruning is the front-line control. We remove affected branches well below the visible damage using sterilized tools so the bacterial infection isn't spread cut to cut. It's routine work for us, and it's most effective when caught early.
